hints: Use continuity of velocity at $t = 6$: $p(6^2) - q(6) = 63 - 4.5(6)$, which gives $36p - 6q = 36$.
Differentiate the velocity function for $0 \le t \le 6$ to get acceleration: $a(t) = 2pt - q$.
Use the condition that acceleration is zero at $t = 2$: $2p(2) - q = 0 \implies q = 4p$, and solve the simultaneous equations for $p$ and $q$.
walkthrough:
State the condition for continuity of velocity at the junction $t = 6\text{ s}$: there are no instantaneous changes in velocity, so the velocity from the quadratic stage must equal the velocity from the linear stage at $t = 6$:
$$v(6^-) = v(6^+)$$
$$p(6^2) - q(6) = 63 - 4.5(6)$$
$$36p - 6q = 63 - 27 = 36$$
Divide both sides by $6$:
$$6p - q = 6\quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Determine the acceleration function for the first stage ($0 \le t \le 6$) by differentiating $v(t)$ with respect to $t$:
$$a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}(pt^2 - qt) = 2pt - q$$

Apply the condition that acceleration is zero when $t = 2\text{ s}$:
$$a(2) = 2p(2) - q = 0$$
$$4p - q = 0 \implies q = 4p\quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Substitute Equation 2 into Equation 1:
$$6p - 4p = 6$$
$$2p = 6$$
Divide by $2$:
$$p = 3$$
Now evaluate $q$:
$$q = 4(3) = 12$$
Thus the values are $p = 3$ and $q = 12$.

hints: For $0 \le t \le 6$, sketch the parabola $v = 3t^2 - 12t = 3t(t - 4)$, passing through $(0,0)$, vertex at $(2,-12)$, and root at $(4,0)$.
For $6 \le t \le 14$, draw a straight line from $(6,36)$ down to $(14,0)$.
walkthrough:
Examine the two piecewise sections of the velocity-time graph:
- For $0 \le t \le 6$: $v(t) = 3t^2 - 12t = 3t(t - 4)$. This is an upward-opening parabola.
  * At $t = 0$: $v(0) = 0$.
  * Turning point (minimum) occurs at $t = 2$: $v(2) = 3(4) - 12(2) = -12$.
  * Intercept on the time axis: $3t(t - 4) = 0 \implies t = 4$, coordinate $(4, 0)$.
  * At junction $t = 6$: $v(6) = 3(36) - 12(6) = 108 - 72 = 36$, coordinate $(6, 36)$.

- For $6 \le t \le 14$: $v(t) = 63 - 4.5t$. This is a linear function (straight line) with constant negative gradient $-4.5$.
  * At $t = 6$: $v(6) = 63 - 27 = 36$, confirming continuity.
  * At $t = 14$: $v(14) = 63 - 4.5(14) = 63 - 63 = 0$, ending at $(14, 0)$.

Draw the complete sketch: a smooth parabola dipping into negative velocities between $0$ and $4$, passing through minimum $(2, -12)$, crossing the axis at $(4, 0)$, reaching $(6, 36)$, followed by a straight line descending uniformly to rest at $(14, 0)$.

hints: Because the velocity is negative between $t = 0$ and $t = 4$, distance travelled requires integrating $|v|$ or splitting the integration at $t = 4$.
Integrate $3t^2 - 12t$ to get $t^3 - 6t^2$. Find the distance from $t = 0$ to $t = 4$: $|[t^3 - 6t^2]_0^4| = |-32| = 32\text{ m}$.
Find the distance from $t = 4$ to $t = 6$: $[t^3 - 6t^2]_4^6 = 0 - (-32) = 32\text{ m}$.
Find the distance from $t = 6$ to $t = 14$ using the area of the triangle: $\frac{1}{2}(8)(36) = 144\text{ m}$, and sum the three distances.
walkthrough:
Note that total distance travelled is the total area between the velocity-time graph and the time axis. Because the velocity is negative for $0 < t < 4$, we must evaluate the distance in separate sections where $v$ does not change sign:
- Section 1: $0 \le t \le 4$ (backward motion, $v \le 0$)
- Section 2: $4 \le t \le 6$ (forward motion, $v \ge 0$)
- Section 3: $6 \le t \le 14$ (forward motion, linear deceleration to rest)

Calculate the distance for Section 1 ($0 \le t \le 4$):
$$s_1 = \left| \int_0^4 (3t^2 - 12t)\,dt \right| = \left| [t^3 - 6t^2]_0^4 \right|$$
$$[4^3 - 6(4^2)] - 0 = 64 - 6(16) = 64 - 96 = -32\text{ m}$$
$$d_1 = |-32| = 32\text{ m}$$

Calculate the distance for Section 3 ($6 \le t \le 14$):
This region is a right-angled triangle with base from $t = 6$ to $t = 14$ (duration $8\text{ s}$) and height $v = 36\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$d_3 = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2}(14 - 6)(36) = \frac{1}{2}(8)(36) = 4(36) = 144\text{ m}$$

Sum all three distances to obtain the total distance travelled:
$$d_{\text{total}} = d_1 + d_2 + d_3 = 32 + 32 + 144 = 208\text{ m}$$
Thus the total distance travelled by particle $P$ during the $14\text{ s}$ is $208\text{ m}$.
